attributes.description: Record -> each environment's synthetic checks. The core turns a canary the environment can run into a cloud-neutral spec: what it requests (HTTPS for health, login page or token; the IdP's start of a SAML sign-in; ldaps:// for a directory bind), how often, its credentials' secret role, the service's exposure, for an internal one the subnets it runs from, the CAs it must trust (the recorded PEMs of the CA certificates the service's certificate chains to, public material added to the runtime's trust store; none recorded: not rendered), or why it can't run. One set of probes (GET following redirects, client-credentials token, LDAPS simple bind; certificates verified) exists as Python and Node.js source. AWS: CloudWatch Synthetics canaries (in the VPC for an internal service, credentials from Secrets Manager). Azure: standard web tests for public GETs needing no private CA, else Container Apps jobs, each with its own identity, running one shared runner given its check as data, by default from an image the organization builds, signs and records by digest; results to Application Insights. Google Cloud: uptime checks for public GETs needing no private CA, else synthetic monitors (Node.js Cloud Run functions, credentials a mounted secret, Direct VPC egress); none in Assured Workloads. Secrets are never rendered; a CA rotation is a record change and a re-render; what can't run is a render note; the checks read back as canary bindings.

attributes.name: canary_specs
attributes.purpose: An environment's canaries whose checked service it binds, as CanarySpecs: name (canary binding else canary), flow, what it requests (https fqdn[:port] + the products' endpoint path for the flow through edge policies; saml-sso: the IdP's saml-start path with the starting SAML integration's entity ID in its query; ldap-bind: ldaps://fqdn:port), interval seconds, credentials secret binding (optional for ldap-bind), keeper, why not rendered, the service name's exposure, for an internal one the subnets its check runs from (the canary binding's ciamSubnetRole, else admitted_subnets), and trust (pki.chain trust_for of the service name's ciamTlsCertificate: the private CA PEMs the check is given, or None); a certificate chaining to CA certificates the record holds none of the PEMs of is a why (with how: record ciamCertificatePem, naming the CA certificates' owners).

attributes.name: script
attributes.purpose: The canary's Python script: its do-not-edit header, the shared probes (observability.probes PYTHON_PROBES: GET, client-credentials token request, LDAPS simple bind) and the CloudWatch Synthetics handler (HANDLER) that reads the canary's Secrets Manager credentials at run time (none: an anonymous LDAP bind) and runs probe(flow, url, creds, CA, CA_PARTIAL), failing the canary when it raises; CA / CA_PARTIAL: the PEMs of the private CA certificates the record holds for the checked service's certificate (spec.trust, pki.chain; None: the runtime's trust store alone) and whether an intermediate is the anchor.

attributes.name: standard
attributes.purpose: Whether an Application Insights standard web test makes a check: a flow one GET answers (core canaries GET_FLOWS: health, login-page, saml-sso) of an internet-facing service name whose certificate needs no CA the check must be given (spec.trust None: a standard test takes no CA certificate); the others are Container Apps jobs (check_jobs).

attributes.name: index_js
attributes.purpose: The synthetic monitor function's index.js: its do-not-edit header (JavaScript comments), the shared Node.js probes (observability.probes NODE_PROBES) and the handler registering SyntheticFunction with runSyntheticHandler: credentials read at each run from the mounted Secret Manager secret (CREDENTIALS = /etc/secrets/check/credentials, null without one), CHECK_CA / CHECK_CA_PARTIAL (the private CA PEMs spec.trust gives, added to Node.js's roots; null: none), probe(flow, url, creds, ca, partial) logged, a rejection failing the monitor.

attributes.name: Trust

attributes.description: Milestone 113 (deferred note 2837 on file 831). As approved (decision 3109, research 3108): a synthetic check of a service whose certificate (ciamTlsCertificate) chains to CA certificates the record holds is given their recorded PEMs (ciamCertificatePem, public material; pki.chain), added to the runtime's own trust store (an intermediate trusted as the anchor when no root is among them): AWS CloudWatch Synthetics (Python, in the script), Azure Container Apps check jobs (CHECK_CA / CHECK_CA_PARTIAL data, image unchanged), GCP synthetic monitors (Node.js index.js). Managed public checks (Azure standard web tests, GCP uptime checks) take no CA: such checks become jobs / monitors. A held chain with no PEM recorded: not rendered, a render note (flow 43, blocker when it feeds an alert) naming the CA (ciamCertAuthority, flow 60), the chain, the CA certificates' owners and what to record. A CA rotation is a record change + re-render. Showcase CHG-2069 (Issuing CA 2's certificate). Departs from the original "by reference read at run time" (premise predated attr 624).
